messages.author: Mike Mazanetz
messages.body:
Dear Forum,
I have been running AMBER and cpptraj without any issues for a while.  I had
my IT dept create a new group for running software, but now I do not seem to
able to run ptraj:
I'm using bash
source $AMBERHOME/amber.sh
$AMBERHOME/bin/cpptraj -p filein.prmtop -I traj.in
$AMBERHOME/bin/cpptraj :  error while loading shared libraries:
libsander.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
The file and folder are where they are meant to be.
Any ideas?  AMBER itself runs just fine.
Thanks,
mike
Honorary Lecturer
School of Natural and Computing Sciences
University of Aberdeen

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Sun, Sep 19, 2021, Mike Mazanetz wrote:
>
>$AMBERHOME/bin/cpptraj :  error while loading shared libraries:
>libsander.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
>
>The file and folder are where they are meant to be.
Can you be a bit more explicit about the last sentence?  Does this mean that
you indeed have an $AMBERHOME/lib/libsander.so file?
What is the value of your LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable?
...thx...dac

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
This is happening because when that particular CPPTRAJ binary was
compiled it was linked with a specific libsander.so. I'm guessing that
the path for libsander.so was changed. You can check what cpptraj is
expecting with `ldd $AMBERHOME/bin/cpptraj`. You may need to recompile
cpptraj so it picks up the new libsander.so location.
-Dan

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
First, if the AMBERHOME directory has been moved, check that AMBERHOME
has been updated to the new location in the $AMBERHOME/amber.sh
script.
Second, ensure that the permissions on the shared library files allow
you to access them (you need r+x I believe). You can check this with
'ls -l <library file>' and 'file <library file>'.
Hope this helps,
-Dan
